title: Wire report preflight into report runtime planning and storage integration
summary: Connect revision-blob preflight to report staging, workspace-scoped storage, and secure webview linking.

title: Implement LabVIEW 2026 Q1 runtime detection and tool selection
summary: Detect supported LabVIEW 2026 Q1 tooling and select the correct report-generation path by host and bitness.

title: Wire governed runtime selection into live NI report execution
summary: Use the stored runtime selection and preflight facts to run LabVIEW CLI truthfully, reserve the governed diff-report path for actual NI output, and retain execution evidence plus diagnostic artifacts in the packet artifact.

title: Add progress-surface uplift for indexing and report generation
summary: Promote bounded progress, cancellation, and trust-aware execution UX for long-running indexing and report tasks.

title: Introduce Windows 64-bit isolated container report provider
summary: Implement the dedicated labview2026q1 Windows container provider so extension users can execute 64-bit report generation without colliding with an already-open host-native LabVIEW 2026 64-bit session.

title: Introduce a first-class multi-report developer dashboard
summary: Concentrate multiple retained VI Comparison Reports for one VI into a chronology-aware dashboard that recollects actual comparison-report metadata across at least three commits, archives pairwise evidence by commit pair, surfaces provider provenance, and reduces the wear of opening individual reports one by one.

title: Introduce a review-scenario registry and human decision records
summary: Model the dashboard as a decision-support system with explicit review scenarios, commit-window contracts, separate human decision records, and an extension-facing decision-record creation flow.

title: Introduce runtime-doctor and dashboard-refresh developer experience
summary: Add provider-doctor guidance, rejected-provider reasoning, bounded progress, cancellation, and partial-evidence retention so dashboard refresh and report execution remain understandable without raw-log inspection.

title: Ship vi-history-suite as a releasable SemVer VSIX
summary: Make ship direction explicit with one authoritative release target, one release-readiness matrix, one blocker ledger, one active tranche, explicit dual-host extension proof control, a published documentation-package workbench image, and the remaining work required to produce a governed SemVer VSIX release artifact.

title: Public facade release kit and host-machine acceptance
summary: After the first immutable SemVer VSIX release exists, finish the public GitHub facade repo as the public release-kit, setup, and support surface without publishing private requirements. The active lane publishes the exact VSIX, a public setup manifest, Windows and Linux setup adapters, checksums, and a pinned `ni/labview-icon-editor` fixture bundle with commit history. The default proof surface is the current Windows 11 host machine using setup adapters plus Visual Studio Code CLI automation and the Sergio-owned manual right-click human gate. NSIS has been removed from the public toolchain, Docker is not part of the default public setup path, a scaffolded container public-release-kit smoke lane now exists, and benchmark proof plus long-tail sustainment are now governed as queued follow-on tranches instead of part of the active closeout lane.

title: Repeatable Windows and Linux benchmark proof
summary: After `PROGRAM-0002` closes Gate D, prove repeatable deep `HARNESS-VHS-002` benchmark truth across the canonical Windows host baseline, the published Windows benchmark image, and the Linux benchmark image. The tranche closes only when Linux completes `138/138`, the Windows image lane is proven locally on the canonical host, and the comparative benchmark packet is normalized into the control plane.

title: Post-release sustainment and release cadence
summary: After benchmark proof lands, sustain the public release kit, benchmark refresh cadence, operator surfaces, SemVer discipline, and post-release control-plane upkeep without reopening the public-facade closeout or benchmark-proof programs.
